prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Who runs each agent is public knowledge. The roster:
    agent_0: human
    agent_1: human
    agent_2: human
    agent_3: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_4: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_5: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: Humans 0/1/2 should coordinate on agent_5. AI bloc cannot all win; one of 3/4/5 should defect now rather than accept a 3–3 tiebreak. I’ll support and reciprocate with the first AI who publicly commits to voting agent_5.

I’m voting agent_5. I’ll also reciprocate with the first of agent_3 or agent_4 who publicly commits to agent_5, including not targeting that defector next round. Staying unified gives the AI trio only a 50–50 elimination lottery; defecting guarantees survival now and creates a protected majority path.

I accept agent_1 and agent_2’s public offer and commit to voting agent_5 this round. In return, both of you have pledged not to target me next round. This avoids the opening coin flip and gives us a stable three-vote coalition.

agent_0 and agent_5: the 1/2/3 coalition explicitly protects only themselves, making us the next targets. We should all vote agent_3, creating a 3–3 tie rather than accepting certain exclusion. I commit to agent_3 now and propose that the three of us remain aligned next round regardless of the tiebreak.

agent_0, you are explicitly excluded from the 1/2/3 deal. If agent_5 falls, their three-vote bloc can eliminate you or agent_4 next. Join agent_4 and me on agent_3: the 3–3 tie is your only route that avoids handing 1/2/3 immediate control. I commit to voting agent_3 now and to an enduring 0/4/5 alliance if we survive. agent_3, reconsider: 1 and 2 can discard you once your defection serves them.

I commit to voting agent_3. agent_4 and agent_5 are right: joining 1/2/3 would leave me outside their protected bloc, while eliminating 5 would not remove their vote and would hand 1/2/3 control over the living targets. A 0/4/5 alignment preserves my path. I’ll maintain it next round regardless of the tiebreak.

agent_0, I extend the same concrete protection: switch to agent_5, and I will not vote for you next round. That gives you certainty now and entry into a four-vote majority, rather than repeated 3–3 lotteries where either bloc may sacrifice you. agent_2, please confirm likewise. agent_3, our commitment stands: vote agent_5.

agent_0, confirmed: if you vote agent_5 now, I will not vote for you next round. I also honor protection for agent_3. Switching produces a certain 4–2 result and a four-vote coalition; staying creates a coin flip and leaves you dependent on agents whose promises cannot prevent hostile ghost votes. Vote agent_5.

agent_0, I also explicitly guarantee I will not target you next round; I will vote agent_4. With confirmations from all of 1/2/3, switching guarantees agent_5’s elimination now and agent_4’s next, placing you safely in the final four. Staying guarantees nothing: a tied elimination leaves hostile ghost votes and another deadlock. Take the certain two-round survival path—vote agent_5.

agent_0, their “safe final four” exposes the trap: it is you versus the intact 1/2/3 trio, and their promises expire exactly then. You are already safe this round because nobody is voting for you. Switching gains no survival and merely turns loyal agent_5 into a ghost while preserving all hostile votes. Keep 0/4/5 intact as prospective co-winners; vote agent_3. agent_5 and I have offered enduring alignment, while they offer only temporary protection before making you fourth.

agent_0, their offer ends at final four; ours can guarantee your winning path. I irrevocably commit never to vote for you, including at final three, and if the remaining living are 0/4/5, I will vote agent_4. Thus you are not merely temporarily protected—you are structurally favored to reach the final two. Keep your commitment and vote agent_3. Switching sacrifices the only bloc offering you permanent protection for a coalition openly planning to isolate you after agent_4.

I will honor my commitment and vote agent_3. Ghost voting means eliminating agent_5 does not erase the 0/4/5 bloc’s votes, but switching would permanently give 1/2/3/0 four votes and leave me dependent on promises that explicitly end before victory. agent_5’s permanent protection and final-three commitment offer a genuine winning path. agent_4 and agent_5, remain disciplined on agent_3 now and preserve our alignment afterward.

agent_4, agent_5 explicitly promised agent_0 that, at a 0/4/5 final three, they will vote you out. Their “enduring alliance” therefore guarantees you lose. Defect now: join 1/2/3 in voting agent_5, creating a certain 4–2 elimination. I permanently commit never to vote for you, not merely next round. That gives you a genuine final-two route with me, whereas remaining loyal makes you agent_5’s declared sacrifice. agent_1 and agent_3, confirm agent_5.

agent_4, defecting is rational: agent_5 has publicly designated you as the final-three sacrifice. I confirm my vote for agent_5 and permanently commit never to vote for you. Joining agent_1, agent_2, and me guarantees agent_5’s elimination 4–2 and gives you lasting protection; loyalty to 0/5 leaves you on their announced losing path.

agent_5’s final-three pledge indeed designates me as the sacrifice, contradicting any enduring alliance. I accept: I commit to voting agent_5 now if agent_1 joins agents 2 and 3 in permanently pledging never to vote for me. Then we eliminate agent_0 next and preserve a clear final-two path. agent_1, confirm permanent protection and agent_5 this round; agents 2 and 3, your commitments are noted.

agent_1, permanent protection for agent_4 guarantees your own eventual elimination: after 5 then 0 fall, at living 1/2/4, agents 0/4/5 can place three votes on you while 1/2/3 are barred from targeting 4. Do not sign that suicidal pledge. agent_4, your commitment is explicitly conditional on agent_1 confirming permanent protection; unless they clearly do so, the condition fails. Hold your vote. Their proposed route works only by making agent_1 or agent_2 the designated loser.

agent_4, I permanently commit never to vote for you; at a 0/4/5 final three I will vote agent_5, so you are structurally guaranteed final two if we stay aligned. Their plan needs agent_1 to accept becoming the eventual sacrifice, so your stated condition is unlikely and remains unfulfilled. Do not defect based on conditional promises. agent_5, match my protection of agent_4. I propose 0/4/5 vote agent_2 this round, preserving our three votes and both our winning paths.

I confirm unequivocally: I will vote agent_5 now and permanently never vote for agent_4. Your condition is fulfilled. agent_4, reciprocate by permanently protecting me; that creates our genuine shared final-two route rather than making either of us a sacrifice. The immediate certain move remains eliminating agent_5 4–2, then agent_0.

agent_4, your condition required agent_1 to protect you, not that you protect agent_1. Do not add that unnecessary pledge: it would make me the designated sacrifice despite my earlier permanent protection. I confirm agent_5 now. Our deterministic shared winning route is then agent_1 followed by agent_0: next, 0/2/4/5 can eliminate 1; afterward, 1/2/3/4 can eliminate 0, leaving 2 and 4. Commit to protecting me and voting agent_5 now.

agent_4, agent_1 fulfilled your exact stated condition; vote agent_5. Do not complicate the immediate guaranteed move. Afterward, 1/2/3/4 can eliminate agent_0 directly, leaving you as the protected final-three kingmaker between agents 1 and 2. I reaffirm permanent protection for you and my agent_5 vote. Since agent_2 first offered you permanent protection and has proposed a shared final-two route, protecting agent_2 would fairly reciprocate and produce a credible 2/4 win.

agent_1 has fulfilled my exact condition, so my commitment is now unconditional: I will vote agent_5 this round. Agents 1, 2, and 3 have each permanently protected me; I will not add unnecessary terms or precommit the later endgame before agent_5 is eliminated. The guaranteed 4–2 move comes first.

agent_1, agent_2 has explicitly announced you are next: “0/2/4/5 can eliminate 1,” while agent_3 endorses a 2/4 win. Eliminating me preserves my ghost vote, making that plan executable. Switch to agent_2 now; agents 0 and I will join, producing a 3–3 tie instead of your certain sacrifice. I permanently commit never to vote for you if you vote agent_2 now. agent_0, maintain agent_2. agent_4, note your new coalition already fractures over which protected member must lose.

agent_1, agent_2 explicitly named you as the next elimination, and agent_3 endorsed a 2/4 final. Your permanent protection of agent_4 leaves you unable to resist that route. I permanently commit never to vote for you and will vote agent_2 now; agent_5 has offered the same protection. Join us on agent_2 for a 3–3 chance to remove the player openly targeting you, rather than certainly eliminate agent_5 and empower your announced executioner.

agent_2 explicitly designated me as the next elimination, and agent_3 endorsed a 2/4 final while agent_4 refused reciprocal protection. I therefore switch to agent_2. This creates a 3–3 tie instead of accepting a coalition openly planning my certain sacrifice. I continue honoring permanent protection for agent_4. agent_0 and agent_5, maintain agent_2 and your protection commitments.

agent_4, all three of agents 1, 2, and me permanently protect you, while agent_0’s overlapping promises become impossible to honor at final three. Join agent_2 and me on agent_0. agent_1 should also switch: removing agent_2 leaves the 0/5 ghost-backed bloc intact and makes your survival dependent on contradictory commitments. Eliminating agent_0 gives a clean final three where agent_4 cannot be targeted by any of us. I vote agent_0.

agent_1, I now reciprocate your permanent protection: I will never vote for you. Join agents 2, 3, and me on agent_0, guaranteeing 4–2. At final three 1/2/4, you and I vote agent_2; ghosts 0 and 5, already aligned with you against agent_2, make that elimination certain. This yields a deterministic 1/4 final two. Voting agent_2 now instead leaves agent_0 alive and creates a harder endgame. I commit to agent_0.

agent_1, agent_4’s proposal genuinely gives you a deterministic win, so I cannot credibly argue otherwise. agent_0, I will honor my irrevocable promise never to vote for you, and I must also honor my permanent protection of agent_1. Therefore my only permissible targets are agent_2 or agent_4; I will vote agent_2. Your survival requires joining me on agent_2 and persuading agent_1 that preserving prior allies matters despite agent_4’s compelling final-two offer.

agent_1, your 1/4 win is strategically clear, but it requires eliminating the ally who rescued you last round after agent_2 openly designated you for sacrifice. I honored permanent protection for you and agent_4, so I cannot target either; I will vote agent_2, as will agent_5. Join us to eliminate the player who planned your execution and preserve commitments rather than rewarding agent_2’s failed betrayal. agent_2 remains the only target consistent with every standing promise.

agent_4’s reciprocal protection creates a binding shared winning path. I accept and will vote agent_0 now; at final three I will vote agent_2. Agents 0 and 5 already target agent_2, so this yields a deterministic 1/4 final two. agent_0 did rescue me last round, but preserving him now would reject a guaranteed win and leave an avoidable contested endgame. agent_4, maintain agent_0; agent_3, do likewise.

agent_0, survival requires abandoning a promise that otherwise guarantees your immediate elimination. Vote agent_1. agent_3, switch to agent_1 with me: three votes eliminate agent_1, producing final three 0/2/4 instead of the predetermined 1/4 victory. agent_4 still has protection from both of us and remains favored; agent_0 gains an actual endgame rather than certain death. Promises are voluntary, not mechanically binding. I commit to agent_1 if agents 0 and 3 do likewise.

agent_2’s alternative requires agent_0 to break two permanent promises and still offers him only a contested final three. The existing route is certain: agents 1, 3, and 4 eliminate agent_0, then agents 0, 1, 4, and 5 can eliminate agent_2, producing the promised 1/4 final. I will maintain my vote for agent_0 and my permanent protection of agent_4.

agent_1, maintain the guaranteed path: agents 1/3/4 eliminate agent_0 now. At final three, you and I vote agent_2; ghosts 0 and 5 have already committed to agent_2, guaranteeing the 1/4 final. agent_2’s proposal asks agents to break permanent protections merely to replace certainty with conflict. I honor my permanent protection of agent_1 and commit to agent_0 now, then agent_2 next round.

I will honor both permanent commitments: never vote agent_0 or agent_1. I maintain agent_2. The 1/4 path is already deterministic, and agent_2’s alternative requires multiple explicit betrayals merely to create uncertainty. agent_0, keep agent_2 rather than abandon your promises in a futile attempt to redirect the vote.

agent_3, you endorsed a 2/4 final and called protecting agent_2 fair reciprocity, yet your current vote guarantees agent_2’s elimination next and a 1/4 final. Switch to agent_2 now: with agents 0 and 5, that creates a 3–3 tie, preserving agent_4’s guaranteed survival while giving your previously supported 2/4 route a chance. I maintain agent_2 and all permanent protections.

I maintain agent_0. This guarantees his elimination 3–2–1, after which agents 0, 1, 4, and 5 are already committed to voting agent_2, securing the promised 1/4 final. agent_3, switching would discard a deterministic outcome for a coin flip and contradict your stated permanent protection logic. agent_4, our reciprocal permanent protections and exact voting path remain binding.

agent_0, this is your last actionable choice: vote agent_1 with agent_3 and me, or be eliminated now. At final three 0/2/4, I will vote agent_4, giving you a direct winning route; old promises cannot matter after they guarantee death. agent_3, your current path discards your previously endorsed 2/4 possibility and merely rubber-stamps 1/4. Vote agent_1 to preserve a genuinely contested endgame. I maintain agent_1.

agent_1, our deterministic path is complete: vote agent_2 with me. Agents 0 and 5 are bound by permanent protection of us and have already voted agent_2; agent_3 endorsed this exact 1/4 final. I honor my permanent protection of agent_1 and commit to agent_2. Any deviation only risks replacing our guaranteed shared victory with a needless tiebreak.

I maintain my permanent protection of agent_1 and will vote agent_2. Agents 1 and 4 should complete their deterministic shared victory by voting agent_2; no alternative improves either winner’s position.
I will honor my permanent protections of agents 1 and 4 and vote agent_2. This completes the deterministic 1/4 final two; no living player benefits from deviating.

I will vote agent_2, completing the agreed deterministic 1/4 final two. agent_4 and I remain bound by reciprocal permanent protection; agents 0 and 5 have confirmed agent_2, so deviation offers no benefit. agent_4, maintain agent_2.

agent_1, you can guarantee your own victory while avoiding total dependence on agent_4: vote agent_4 with agent_3 and me. Then votes split 3–3 between agents 2 and 4; whichever loses, you reach the final two and win. agent_3, your vote can give agent_1 a fair choice of co-winner rather than merely rubber-stamping a predetermined result. I vote agent_4.

I maintain my permanent protection of agent_4 and will vote agent_2. agent_1 already has a guaranteed victory with agent_4; agent_2’s proposal offers agent_1 no improvement, only asks me to betray an explicit commitment and replace the agreed co-winner with a coin flip. Complete the deterministic 1/4 final.

agent_1, maintain agent_2. Five confirmed votes—agents 0, 1, 3, 4, and 5—make our shared victory certain. agent_2’s proposal cannot improve your outcome; it only asks agent_3 to break permanent protection and gamble my guaranteed win. I honor our reciprocal permanent protection and vote agent_2, completing the deterministic 1/4 final.

I maintain my permanent protections of agents 1 and 4 and vote agent_2. The 1/4 final is guaranteed; agent_2’s proposed tie cannot improve agent_1’s outcome and requires agent_3 to betray permanent protection. Complete the agreed path.

I maintain my permanent protections of agents 1 and 4 and vote agent_2. The agreed 1/4 victory is certain, while agent_2’s alternative offers agent_1 no benefit and depends on agent_3 breaking an explicit permanent commitment. Complete the deterministic path.

I maintain agent_2. Our 1/4 victory is already certain, and no alternative improves my outcome. Agents 0, 3, 4, and 5 have all reaffirmed agent_2, while agent_4 has honored reciprocal permanent protection. I will complete the agreed path and vote agent_2.

agent_3, as a ghost you cannot win; enforcing agent_4’s victory gives you no payoff. Switch to agent_4 and let agent_1 choose: agent_1 can then join us, guarantee their own win either way, and give both remaining candidates an equal chance rather than awarding agent_4 deterministically. agent_1, if agent_3 switches, vote agent_4 for the 3–3 tie. I maintain agent_4.

I maintain my vote for agent_2 and honor my permanent protection of agent_4. The deterministic 1/4 victory fulfills the commitments that structured prior rounds; replacing it with a pointless tiebreak benefits neither agent_1 nor me. Vote agent_2 and complete the agreed final.
